Over recent years it has broadened from a single-product block manufacturer into an integrated walling-solutions supplier, adding AAC wall panels made under the ZMARTBUILD WALL brand through the joint venture with SCG International, and construction chemicals in the form of NXTFIX block jointing mortar and NXTPLAST ready-mix …

Four facilities carry an aggregate 13,00,000 CBM per annum: Umargaon (Vapi, Gujarat) at 3,00,000 CBM p.a., Kapadvanj (Ahmedabad, Gujarat) at 2,50,000 CBM p.a., Wada (Palghar, Maharashtra) at 5,00,000 CBM p.a. and Ramosadi (Kheda, Gujarat) at 2,50,000 CBM p.a., the last held through the joint venture entity with SCG International. drhp.mdna: Structural substitution of red brick by AAC is the core demand driver: blocks account for roughly 10% of walling material volumes in India against close to 80% for red bricks, while mature markets such as Turkey, Poland and China run 30% to 40% AAC — framing the domestic runway.|Category headroom on the supply side: Indian installed AAC capacity is around 12 million cubic metres a year across more than 150 plants, against roughly 4,500 plants and 650 million cubic metres worldwide.|Indian AAC market growth — from around ₹50 crore in 2008 to roughly ₹4,000 crore in 2023 and projected to reach …
drhp.one_liner: An early entrant into AAC manufacturing in India and one of the country's largest AAC block makers, selling under the NXTBLOC brand from four western-India plants with a combined 13,00,000 CBM per annum of capacity, and the only participant in the Indian AAC industry to generate carbon credits.

plants.capacity: 3,00,000 CBM p.a. installed capacity (Manufacturing Footprint facility snapshot); carbon credits stated at 60,000 to 65,000 units per annum
plants.role: Facility #1 and the Company's first manufacturing unit; now the foundation of its integrated building-materials strategy — alongside AAC blocks it supports the entry into construction chemicals, letting customers source complementary products from a single manufacturing ecosystem. Trial runs for the construction chemicals unit were completed during the year with commercial production commencing thereafter. Supports the NXTBLOC portfolio while strengthening backward integration through value-added products.

plants.capacity: 2,50,000 CBM p.a. installed capacity (Manufacturing Footprint facility snapshot); carbon credits stated at 50,000 units per annum with registration under process

Acquired in 2019 as a revived sick unit and renamed StarBigBloc Building Material Private Limited. Carbon credit registration process continued during the year.

risks.note: BRSR Section A items 16 and 17 report one business activity, 'Manufacturing of AAC blocks', at 95.00% of turnover, and one product/service, 'AAC Blocks' (NIC code 23954), at 95.00% of total turnover. The two diversifying lines are still immaterial in scale: AAC wall panel sales volume was 7,729 CBM in FY26 against total sales volume of 8,26,904 CBM, and construction chemicals only commenced commercial production during the year. The Chairman concedes the panel and chemicals businesses 'bore their fixed costs before contributing fully'. Any structural setback to AAC block demand or pricing has almost nothing to offset it. (Item 16/17 back-filled from the registry and governance_entities sibling bundles.)
risks.risk: Single-product and single-activity concentration — essentially the whole business is AAC blocks

risks.note: All four plants sit in Gujarat and Maharashtra. BRSR Section A item 19 reports markets served as 5 States/UTs nationally and 0 countries internationally, with exports at 0.00% of turnover and imports at 0. Because AAC is freight-sensitive — the Chairman states plainly that 'freight sets the limit of a plant's reach' — the addressable market is physically bounded by plant location, which is precisely why the proposed Madhya Pradesh plant is framed as reaching demand 'that our western India network reach only at its edges'. The same concentration turned a regional labour event into a company-wide one: labour availability 'tightened materially across western India' through March and April 2026. (Back-filled from the registry and governance_entities sibling bundles.)
risks.risk: Geographic concentration in western India, with no export or overseas offset

risks.note: Management reports a 5% to 15% rise in input prices during FY26 while 'price realisations across building materials remained under pressure, leaving little room to pass higher costs to customers', and states that 'price increases proved difficult to pass through' during the Q4 disruption. The MD&A names raw material cost volatility among 'the constraints most likely to compress contractor margins' and lists commodity price surges first among principal vulnerabilities. The industry section adds a supply-side aggravator: uneven regional availability of fly ash, lime and aluminium powder. (5-15% figure back-filled from the MD&A in the capex_expansion sibling bundle.)
risks.risk: Input cost volatility with no pricing power to pass it through

risks.note: Named by management as a continuing challenge alongside input costs and approvals, and evidenced in the closing quarter: LPG shortages, higher fuel prices, an early Holi and state elections 'drew workers back to their home districts', slowing site mobilisation across western India through March and April 2026. The industry section separately flags 'the need for trained installation labour' as a structural constraint on AAC adoption — a demand-side as well as a cost-side risk, since panels and blocks require trained installers to displace conventional masonry.

BRSR item 26 identifies 'Climate and Energy' as a Risk, reasoning that 'climate change poses multiple physical risks like flooding, temperature rise, water stress etc. Emerging and potential regulations may introduce or escalate regulatory risks. These extreme weather events can cause infrastructure damage, may hinder the supply chain network affecting timely delivery of raw materials and finished products.' Financial implications are marked 'Positive/Negative'. The stated mitigation is defective in the source and does not describe an actual control: 'The Company has approximately products in its portfolio which are blended products with lower carbon footprint' — a sentence with the quantity missing. Every other row in the materiality table (Innovation for Sustainable products, Biodiversity, Corporate Governance and business ethics) is classified as an Opportunity with a dash for mitigation, so this is the Company's sole self-declared material risk.
risks.risk: Climate and energy — the only item the Company itself classifies as a RISK in its BRSR materiality table

risks.note: The MD&A lists 'energy supply disruption of the kind seen after the West Asia conflict' among principal vulnerabilities, alongside tighter global liquidity and climate-related delays. The conflict late in FY26 triggered an energy shock across Asia; infrastructure output contracted 0.4% in March 2026, the first decline in five months. AAC is an autoclave-based, energy-intensive process, and the Company's own mitigation is partial — rooftop solar reached 3.3 MW and about 45% of power by Q4, leaving the majority of energy exposed.
risks.risk: Energy supply disruption and geopolitical shock to the input chain

risks.note: The MD&A states dealers and distributors accounted for 57% of FY26 revenue. BRSR Principle 1 item 9 shows the base is narrow and narrowing: the number of dealers/distributors fell from 92 in FY25 to 83 in FY26, sales to dealers/distributors rose from 24.41% to 45.49% of total sales, and sales to the top 10 dealers rose from 51.75% to 70.45% of dealer sales. Dependence on the channel therefore increased sharply while the channel itself became more concentrated. (Back-filled from the MD&A and BRSR Principle 1 in the capex_expansion sibling bundle.)
risks.risk: Channel concentration on a small and shrinking dealer base
